newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Tsum plans issue level one ADRs in 97.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Tsum plans issue level one ADRs in 97.

text.p: Russian retail group Tsum plans to issue level one American Depositary Receipts on its shares in 1997, financial advisers to the company said on Thursday.
"Preliminary work on an issue of ADRs has already been done," said Oleg Yachnik, president of investment company Olma, which acts as financial adviser to Tsum.
Yachkin said the issue would not be a private placement.
AO Torgovy Dom Tsum recently issued 30 million shares at 2,000 roubles each to raise some $11 million for modernisation.
Before the issue, Tsum was 24.5 percent owned by the Moscow city government, Swiss private bank Pictet & Cie had 6.71 percent, Olma had 5.03 percent and AOOT Russ-Invest had 5.5 percent.
Several Russian companies have already issued ADRs, securities which allow overseas investors to access foreign shares without settlement problems in the issuer's market.
Tsum shares had not traded on the Russian Trading System by 1230 GMT. They closed on Monday at $0.361.
